title: AGENTS.md — ggseg.formats
text: Built validated ggseg_atlas() constructor ggseg_atlas.R — treat constructor authoritative signature, argument list copied . Conceptually atlas classed list : atlas — short name string (e.g. "dk"). type — atlas kind, drawn fixed set (currently "cortical", "subcortical", "tract", "cerebellar") enforced match.arg() constructor; extend new type ever added. drives subclass tag (paste0(type, "_atlas")). palette — named character vector hex colours, keyed label. core — data.frame, one row per region, required columns hemi, region, label; may carry extra metadata columns (lobe, network, Brodmann, …). data — ggseg_atlas_data object matching type, built per-type constructors ggseg_atlas_data.R. class vector c("<type>_atlas", "ggseg_atlas", "list"). Preserve ordering — per-type is_*_atlas() predicates rely subclass tag, ggseg_atlas validity check revalidates structure constructor (wrong--classed object rejected). contract; extend behaviour adding accessors rather reshaping object.

title: Customising brain atlases
text: ggseg.formats provides three groups manipulation functions. Region functions (atlas_region_*) control regions active atlas. View functions (atlas_view_*) control 2D sf geometry—views present arranged. Core functions (atlas_core_*) enrich region metadata. accept ggseg_atlas first argument, return new ggseg_atlas, play nicely pipe.

title: Customising brain atlases
text: atlas_region_remove() strips region entirely—core, palette, sf geometry, 3D data. pattern argument passed grepl() ignore.case = TRUE, partial matches work: atlas_region_keep() inverse: keeps regions match turns everything else context geometry (sf preserved surface continuity, non-matching regions leave core palette): functions accept match_on argument choose whether pattern matches "region" (default, human-readable name) "label" (unique identifier):
code: no_cc <- atlas_region_remove(dk(), "corpus callosum") "corpus callosum" %in% atlas_regions(no_cc) #> [1] FALSE frontal <- atlas_region_keep(dk(), "frontal") atlas_regions(frontal) #> [1] "caudal middle frontal"  "frontal pole"           "lateral orbitofrontal"  #> [4] "medial orbitofrontal"   "rostral middle frontal" "superior frontal" lh_only <- atlas_region_keep(dk(), "^lh_", match_on = "label") head(atlas_labels(lh_only)) #> [1] "lh_bankssts"                "lh_caudalanteriorcingulate" #> [3] "lh_caudalmiddlefrontal"     "lh_corpuscallosum"          #> [5] "lh_cuneus"                  "lh_entorhinal"

title: Customising brain atlases
text: Sometimes want region’s polygon stay visible (rendered grey) appear legend carry data. atlas_region_contextual() . removes region core, palette, 3D data leaves sf geometry place: Compare atlas_region_remove(), delete ventricle polygons entirely, leaving gaps 2D slices.
code: ctx <- atlas_region_contextual(aseg(), "ventricle") "lateral ventricle" %in% atlas_regions(ctx) #> [1] FALSE

title: Customising brain atlases
text: atlas_region_rename() changes region column without touching label (geometry links stay intact). Pass fixed string: pass function programmatic renaming:
code: renamed <- atlas_region_rename(   dk(),   "banks of superior temporal sulcus",   "STS banks" ) "STS banks" %in% atlas_regions(renamed) #> [1] TRUE upper <- atlas_region_rename(dk(), ".*", toupper) head(atlas_regions(upper)) #> [1] "BANKS OF SUPERIOR TEMPORAL SULCUS" "CAUDAL ANTERIOR CINGULATE"         #> [3] "CAUDAL MIDDLE FRONTAL"             "CORPUS CALLOSUM"                   #> [5] "CUNEUS"                            "ENTORHINAL"

title: Customising brain atlases
text: atlas_views() tells 2D views atlas : atlas_view_keep() atlas_view_remove() filter views pattern. want sagittal slice: remove several views passing vector:
code: atlas_views(aseg()) #> [1] "axial_3"   "axial_4"   "axial_5"   "axial_6"   "coronal_1" "coronal_2" #> [7] "sagittal" sag <- atlas_view_keep(aseg(), "sagittal") atlas_views(sag) #> [1] "sagittal" fewer <- atlas_view_remove(aseg(), c("axial_3", "coronal_2")) atlas_views(fewer) #> [1] "axial_4"   "axial_5"   "axial_6"   "coronal_1" "sagittal"

title: Customising brain atlases
text: filtering regions may small polygon fragments left —tiny slivers region just barely crossed slice plane. atlas_view_remove_small() removes region polygons minimum area threshold. Context polygons (core) never removed: can scope removal specific views: atlas_view_remove_region() removes specific region’s sf geometry without touching core, palette, 3D data. useful region’s 2D projection misleading still want 3D:
code: cleaned <- atlas_view_remove_small(aseg(), min_area = 50) #> ℹ Removed 20 geometries below area 50 cleaned_sag <- atlas_view_remove_small(   aseg(),   min_area = 50,   views = "sagittal" ) #> ℹ Removed 2 geometries below area 50 no_stem_sf <- atlas_view_remove_region(   aseg(),   "brain stem",   match_on = "region" )

title: Customising brain atlases
text: remove views, remaining geometry keeps original coordinates, can leave awkward gaps. atlas_view_gather() repositions views side--side configurable gap: atlas_view_reorder() lets choose left--right order repositions time. Views mentioned order appended end:
code: trimmed <- aseg() |>   atlas_view_keep(c("sagittal", "coronal_3", "axial_3")) |>   atlas_view_gather() atlas_views(trimmed) #> [1] "axial_3"  "sagittal" reordered <- aseg() |>   atlas_view_keep(c("sagittal", "coronal_3", "axial_3")) |>   atlas_view_reorder(c("axial_3", "sagittal", "coronal_3")) atlas_views(reordered) #> [1] "axial_3"  "sagittal"

title: Customising brain atlases
text: atlas_core_add() left-joins data frame onto core table. useful attaching grouping variables, statistical results, per-region information. add custom network column handful regions: argument defaults "region" can join shared column.
code: network_info <- data.frame(   region = c(     "superior frontal",     "precuneus",     "inferior parietal",     "posterior cingulate"   ),   network = "default mode" ) enriched <- atlas_core_add(dk(), network_info) enriched$core[!is.na(enriched$core$network), c("region", "network")] #>                 region      network #> 8    inferior parietal default mode #> 23 posterior cingulate default mode #> 25           precuneus default mode #> 28    superior frontal default mode #> 43   inferior parietal default mode #> 58 posterior cingulate default mode #> 60           precuneus default mode #> 63    superior frontal default mode

title: The ggseg_atlas object
text: five slots accessed $: $atlas short name (used look atlases string) $type one "cortical", "subcortical", "tract". $palette named character vector mapping labels hex colours: $core data frame one row per region. always region label columns, often include hemi additional metadata like lobe structure: Finally, $data ggseg_atlas_data object holds actual geometry. contents depend atlas type.
code: dk()$atlas #> [1] "dk" dk()$type #> [1] "cortical" head(dk()$palette) #>                lh_bankssts lh_caudalanteriorcingulate  #>                  "#196428"                  "#7D64A0"  #>     lh_caudalmiddlefrontal          lh_corpuscallosum  #>                  "#641900"                  "#784632"  #>                  lh_cuneus              lh_entorhinal  #>                  "#DC1464"                  "#DC140A" head(dk()$core) #>   hemi                            region                      label #> 1 left banks of superior temporal sulcus                lh_bankssts #> 2 left         caudal anterior cingulate lh_caudalanteriorcingulate #> 3 left             caudal middle frontal     lh_caudalmiddlefrontal #> 4 left                   corpus callosum          lh_corpuscallosum #> 5 left                            cuneus                  lh_cuneus #> 6 left                        entorhinal              lh_entorhinal #>           lobe #> 1     temporal #> 2    cingulate #> 3      frontal #> 4 white matter #> 5    occipital #> 6     temporal class(dk()$data) #> [1] "ggseg_data_cortical" "ggseg_atlas_data"

title: The ggseg_atlas object
text: ggseg.formats ships three atlases illustrate three types. Cortical atlases like dk parcellate cortical surface. data object ggseg_data_cortical containing sf polygons 2D rendering vertex indices 3D: Subcortical atlases like aseg represent deep brain structures. data ggseg_data_subcortical sf polygons individual 3D meshes: Tract atlases like tracula represent white matter bundles. data ggseg_data_tract sf polygons centerlines generate tube meshes 3D: every case sf component drives 2D plotting type-specific component (vertices, meshes, centerlines) drives 3D.
code: dk()$type #> [1] "cortical" names(dk()$data) #> [1] "sf"       "vertices" "polygons" aseg()$type #> [1] "subcortical" names(aseg()$data) #> [1] "sf"       "meshes"   "polygons" tracula()$type #> [1] "tract" names(tracula()$data) #> [1] "sf"          "centerlines" "polygons"

title: The ggseg_atlas object
text: $core data frame single source truth regions atlas contains. Every manipulation function updates core first propagates changes geometry palette. required columns region (human-readable name) label (unique identifier links core geometry). atlases also carry hemi: atlases include additional metadata columns. dk atlas, instance, lobe: can add metadata atlas_core_add() (covered manipulation vignette).
code: str(dk()$core) #> Classes 'tbl_df', 'tbl' and 'data.frame':    70 obs. of  4 variables: #>  $ hemi  : chr  "left" "left" "left" "left" ... #>  $ region: chr  "banks of superior temporal sulcus" "caudal anterior cingulate" "caudal middle frontal" "corpus callosum" ... #>  $ label : chr  "lh_bankssts" "lh_caudalanteriorcingulate" "lh_caudalmiddlefrontal" "lh_corpuscallosum" ... #>  $ lobe  : chr  "temporal" "cingulate" "frontal" "white matter" ... unique(dk()$core$lobe) #> [1] "temporal"     "cingulate"    "frontal"      "white matter" "occipital"    #> [6] "parietal"     "insula"

title: Migrating atlas packages to sf-optional
text: walks directory, loads .rda, finds every atlas object inside, converts geom brain_polygons, drops legacy sf/polygons slots, saves file back xz compression. Files nothing migrate left untouched, reports changed: conversion reads sf coordinates, sf must installed machine run migration . one-time maintainer step; published package longer needs sf. idempotent — running twice -op already-migrated files, safe wire data-raw/ build script.
code: ggseg.formats::migrate_atlas_files("data") #> ✔ Migrated `dk.rda`. #> ✔ Migrated `aseg.rda`. #> ℹ Skipped `palette.rda` (nothing to migrate).

title: Migrating atlas packages to sf-optional

code: ggseg.formats::migrate_atlas_files("data", keep_sf = TRUE)

what: Brain Atlas Data Structures for the ggsegverse Ecosystem
title: Brain Atlas Data Structures for the ggsegverse Ecosystem
text: ggseg.formats provides ggseg_atlas S3 class powers ggsegverse ecosystem 2D 3D brain visualisation. ships four bundled atlases, set accessor functions querying atlas contents, pipe-friendly manipulation API subsetting, renaming, enriching atlas objects.

title: Brain Atlas Data Structures for the ggsegverse Ecosystem
text: package includes four atlases covering main atlas types: dk — Desikan-Killiany cortical parcellation (68 regions) aseg — FreeSurfer automatic subcortical segmentation tracula — TRACULA white matter tract atlas suit — SUIT cerebellar lobular atlas
code: library(ggseg.formats) plot(dk()) plot(aseg()) plot(tracula()) plot(suit())

title: Brain Atlas Data Structures for the ggsegverse Ecosystem
text: Atlas objects designed exploration customisation. can query regions, filter views, pipe operations together:
code: aseg_small <- aseg() |>   atlas_region_keep("hippocampus|amygdala|thalamus") |>   atlas_view_keep("coronal_3|axial_3") |>   atlas_view_gather() plot(aseg_small)

text: Functions modifying brain atlas objects. cover three areas:

title: Manipulate brain atlas regions and views — atlas_manipulation
code: atlas_region_remove(atlas, pattern, match_on = c("region", "label"))  atlas_region_contextual(   atlas,   pattern,   match_on = c("region", "label"),   ignore.case = TRUE )  atlas_region_op(   atlas,   x,   y,   action = c("difference", "intersection", "union", "symdifference"),   into = NULL,   match_on = c("label", "region"),   colour = NULL )  atlas_context_remove(atlas)  atlas_region_rename(atlas, pattern, replacement)  atlas_region_keep(atlas, pattern, match_on = c("region", "label"))  atlas_core_add(atlas, data, by = "region")  atlas_view_remove(atlas, views)  atlas_view_keep(atlas, views)  atlas_view_remove_region(   atlas,   pattern,   match_on = c("label", "region"),   views = NULL )  atlas_view_remove_small(atlas, min_area, views = NULL)  atlas_view_gather(atlas, gap = 0.15)  atlas_view_reorder(atlas, order, gap = 0.15)

title: Manipulate brain atlas regions and views — atlas_manipulation
text: atlas ggseg_atlas object pattern Character pattern match. Uses grepl(..., ignore.case = TRUE). match_on Column match : "region" "label". ignore.case atlas_region_contextual(): passed grepl(). Defaults TRUE backwards compatibility, note context pattern like "Thalamus" also matches focus labels "hypothalamus"; set FALSE (/anchor pattern) matters. x, y atlas_region_op(): patterns selecting two operands. action atlas_region_op(): boolean operation apply. atlas_region_op(): label result region. colour atlas_region_op(): optional fill . supplied, registered core palette; NULL, result contextual geometry . replacement atlas_region_rename(): replacement string function. data atlas_core_add(): data.frame metadata join. atlas_core_add(): column(s) join . Default "region". views view functions: character vector view names patterns. Multiple values collapsed "|" matching. min_area atlas_view_remove_small(): minimum polygon area keep. Context geometries never removed. gap Proportional gap views (default 0.15 = 15% max width). order atlas_view_reorder(): character vector desired view order. Unspecified views appended end.

title: Manipulate brain atlas regions and views — atlas_manipulation
text: Modified ggseg_atlas object

title: Manipulate brain atlas regions and views — atlas_manipulation
text: Region manipulation modifies regions active atlas: atlas_region_remove(): completely remove regions atlas_region_contextual(): keep geometry remove core/palette atlas_context_remove(): drop contextual sf geometry atlas_region_rename(): rename regions core atlas_region_keep(): keep matching regions atlas_region_op(): combine two regions' geometry boolean op (difference / intersection / union / symdifference) View manipulation modifies 2D sf geometry data: atlas_view_remove(): remove entire views atlas_view_keep(): keep matching views atlas_view_remove_region(): remove specific region geometry sf atlas_view_remove_small(): remove small polygon fragments atlas_view_gather(): reposition views close gaps atlas_view_reorder(): change view order Core manipulation modifies atlas metadata: atlas_core_add(): join additional metadata columns

title: Manipulate brain atlas regions and views — atlas_manipulation
text: atlas_region_contextual(): Keep geometry visual context remove core, palette, 3D data. Context geometries render grey appear legends. Contextual rows moved behind remaining core regions focus regions draw top overlap projection. Operates whichever 2D representation atlas carries (sf /polygons), keeping sync, needs sf polygon atlas. atlas_region_op(): Combine two sets region geometry vector boolean operation (per view), writing result new region . x y patterns matched match_on; within view matching geometries unioned, combined via action: "difference" (x minus y, e.g. punching white matter cortex silhouette), "intersection", "union", "symdifference". Inputs left place; existing geometry replaced. colour, becomes legended core region; otherwise stays contextual (grey) drawn behind core regions. Boolean ops need geometry engine, one manipulation helper always requires sf installed; polygon-atlas rehydrated operation result returned polygon form. atlas_context_remove(): Drop contextual sf geometry — every sf row whose label present core. Covers labels marked via atlas_region_contextual() plus pipeline-generated outlines (cortex_, Background, unknown). Remaining views re-packed via atlas_view_gather() plot focuses tightly labelled regions. atlas_region_rename(): Rename regions matching pattern. affects region column, label. replacement function, receives matched names returns new names. atlas_region_keep(): Keep matching regions. Non-matching regions removed core, palette, 3D data sf geometry preserved surface continuity. atlas_core_add(): Join additional metadata columns atlas core. atlas_view_remove(): Remove views matching pattern sf data. Remaining views re-packed via atlas_view_gather() layout stays tight. atlas_view_keep(): Keep views matching pattern. atlas_view_remove_region(): Remove specific region geometry sf data . Core, palette, 3D data unchanged. Views re-packed via atlas_view_gather() case view shrank. atlas_view_remove_small(): Remove region geometries minimum area threshold. Context geometries (labels core) never removed. Optionally scope specific views. Views re-packed via atlas_view_gather() case view shrank. atlas_view_gather(): Reposition remaining views close gaps view removal. atlas_view_reorder(): Reorder views reposition. Views order appended end.

text: Extracts coordinates sf-backed atlas geometry table returns nested data.frame keyed label. row carries geometry list-column containing per-view, per-ring point coordinates needed render graphics::polypath() (using subgroup ring index holes).

title: Convert an sf atlas geometry to the sf-optional polygon format — sf_to_polygons
code: sf_to_polygons(sf_data)

title: Convert an sf atlas geometry to the sf-optional polygon format — sf_to_polygons
text: sf_data sf-class data.frame columns label, view, geometry (sfc MULTIPOLYGON).

title: Convert an sf atlas geometry to the sf-optional polygon format — sf_to_polygons
text: data.frame one row per label geometry list-column. nested element data.frame columns view, x, y, group (disjoint polygon piece within label/view), subgroup (ring within piece; first = exterior, rest = holes). Internal conversion primitive. atlas-level public API use as_polygon_atlas() / atlas_polygons().

title: SUIT Cerebellar Lobular Atlas — suit
text: Returns SUIT cerebellar parcellation (Diedrichsen et al., 2009): cerebellar cortex split anatomical lobules plus deep nuclei (dentate, interposed, fastigial).

title: SUIT Cerebellar Lobular Atlas — suit
code: suit()

title: SUIT Cerebellar Lobular Atlas — suit
text: ggseg_atlas object components: atlas Character. Atlas name ("suit") type Character. Atlas type ("cerebellar") palette Named character vector colours region data ggseg_data_cerebellar object containing: geom brain_polygons table 2D rendering vertices Vertex indices surface lobules meshes Per-structure 3D meshes deep nuclei

title: SUIT Cerebellar Lobular Atlas — suit
text: Surface lobules carry vertex indices shared SUIT cerebellar mesh (see get_cerebellar_mesh()); deep nuclei carry individual 3D meshes. 2D geometry stored sf-optional polygon (geom) representation, atlas renders ggseg without requiring sf installed.

title: SUIT Cerebellar Lobular Atlas — suit
text: Diedrichsen J, Balsters JH, Flavell J, et al. (2009). probabilistic MR atlas human cerebellum. NeuroImage, 46(1):39-46. doi:10.1016/j.neuroimage.2009.01.045

title: SUIT Cerebellar Lobular Atlas — suit

title: TRACULA White Matter Tract Atlas — tracula
text: Returns TRACULA (TRActs Constrained UnderLying Anatomy) white matter bundle atlas MNI space.

code: tracula()

title: TRACULA White Matter Tract Atlas — tracula
text: ggseg_atlas object components: atlas Character. Atlas name ("tracula") type Character. Atlas type ("tract") palette Named character vector colours tract data ggseg_data_tract object containing: centerlines List centerline matrices per tract sf Simple features data frame 2D rendering

title: TRACULA White Matter Tract Atlas — tracula
text: atlas contains major white matter tracts reconstructed diffusion MRI using FreeSurfer's TRACULA training data. works ggseg (2D slice projections) ggseg3d (3D tube mesh visualizations).

title: TRACULA White Matter Tract Atlas — tracula
text: Yendiki , Panneck P, Srinivasan P, et al. (2011). Automated probabilistic reconstruction white-matter pathways health disease using atlas underlying anatomy. Frontiers Neuroinformatics, 5:23. doi:10.3389/fninf.2011.00023
